verdict:
AVOID — and NOT a value case at all (blue PARTIALLY OVERTURNED red, both 8/10). The screen admitted CELH on the deepest drawdown in the batch (-71.7% vs its own 3y high, well past the winners' -46% median) and the courts found the depth is the business breaking, not the multiple compressing — which is the exact fallen-compounder-vs-melting-ice-cube distinction this lane exists to draw, arrived at without the frame being followed.

WHAT SURVIVES CONFIRMED: the flagship Celsius brand is in ABSOLUTE decline (-4.2% H1); the growth that remains is BOUGHT — organic promotional escalation of ~+650bps isolated in Q2, which is the real margin mechanism; related-party concentration 60.2% AND RISING; $56.2M/yr of senior preferred dividends ahead of the common; a $101.1M adjudicated judgment.

RED'S STRONGEST KILL, which blue did not disturb and which is structural rather than cyclical: the common is a RESIDUAL behind a counterparty that is simultaneously the distributor, ~59% of revenue, the holder of $1.76B of mezzanine paper, and the subject of the securities litigation — and $598.8M of the balance sheet is a CAPITALIZED PAYMENT TO THAT SAME DISTRIBUTOR, amortized against revenue for seventeen years, on a book where goodwill plus that asset already exceeds total common equity. Any renegotiation of the Pepsi agreement is simultaneously a revenue event, an impairment event, a litigation event AND a senior-claim event on ONE counterparty: four correlated hits to a negative-tangible-book residual. Unbounded tail, live today.

WHAT DID NOT SURVIVE (blue's corrections): the 'Alani is decelerating' leg is refuted — it grew +21% YoY; the $9.40B EV was overstated (corrected $8.88B ~ 12.7x EBITDA, i.e. a MARKET multiple on a shrinking flagship, not a discount); litigation-as-open-threat and the tangible-book alarm both overstated. Note red's 'no broker quote' complaint was partly self-inflicted — the pack's own tape is broker-sourced.
